difficulty_reason: Connect OAuth registration uses dashboard settings, a Stripe-issued client_id and registered redirect URIs; implementing the connection flow and meeting marketplace requirements are separate work.
setup_time: unknown - Stripe documents no registration timeline; enabling OAuth and getting a test client_id is self-serve in the dashboard, while live mode requires completing account activation (business verification), whose duration is undocumented

approval.kind: Connect OAuth setup is documented as self-serve without a review step; publishing a Stripe App on the App Marketplace requires review.
approval.wait: 4 business days for the marketplace app review (documented); resubmission and re-review are required after changes to the app or listing
approval.notes: Keep the two products separate. Connect OAuth links Standard accounts to a platform. Stripe documents enabling OAuth in Connect settings, obtaining a client_id and registering redirect URIs, but does not describe a separate app-review step in that flow. This is not proof that every live platform is automatically approved: account activation and service requirements still apply. Stripe does not recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms and points to Connect Onboarding instead. Public Stripe Apps use a separate marketplace publishing process, including review and the marketplace OAuth v2 install link. Apps shared only with members of your own Stripe account do not go through review.
approval.wait_short: no separate Connect OAuth review documented; marketplace feedback in 4 business days

summary: Choose the Stripe product first. Connect OAuth links Standard accounts to a platform through Connect settings, but Stripe recommends Connect Onboarding instead for new platforms. Stripe Apps have a separate distribution and authentication path: marketplace publication requires review, with an approval or feedback email documented in 4 business days; private team-only apps skip that review. Live-mode activation is a separate gate.

steps.title: Choose your path before touching settings
steps.detail: For a new Connect platform, Stripe recommends Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts instead of OAuth. A Stripe App has a separate marketplace distribution and authentication path; do not treat Connect OAuth registration as Stripe App registration.

steps.title: Activate your Stripe account for live mode
steps.detail: Sandboxes work immediately for testing. To use any service in live mode you must verify your business and complete activation requirements; marketplace publishing additionally requires a verified email and business details.

steps.title: Enable OAuth in Connect settings and copy your client_id
steps.detail: In the dashboard's Connect OAuth onboarding options, enable onboarding accounts with OAuth, copy the Stripe-generated client_id (separate live and test IDs exist; use the sandbox client_id against sandbox accounts), and register every redirect URI - Stripe falls back to the first configured URI when the parameter is omitted.

steps.title: Build the connection flow
steps.detail: Send users to connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, your client_id, scope=read_write (platforms MUST use read_write; read_only is reserved for registered extensions and omission errors out), and a unique state value for CSRF protection. Users with no Stripe account create one inside the authorization flow.

steps.title: Exchange the code once and store the account ID
steps.detail: POST the short-lived, single-use authorization code to connect.stripe.com/oauth/token with your secret API key in the matching test/live mode. Store stripe_user_id, then make requests using your platform key and the Stripe-Account header. The OAuth reference marks access_token and refresh_token as deprecated. Do not retry a consumed code: consuming it more than once revokes the account connection.

steps.title: Handle disconnection both ways
steps.detail: Watch the account.application.deauthorized webhook to clean up when a user disconnects you, and offer disconnect yourself by POSTing client_id and stripe_user_id to connect.stripe.com/oauth/deauthorize.

steps.title: For a marketplace listing, pass the app review
steps.detail: Submit the listing using the live-mode public install URL for marketplace OAuth v2, not Connect onboarding. Provide test accounts (not real accounts), complete testing guidance, and either disable MFA on those test accounts or explain how reviewers can pass it. Recordings help explain complex flows. Stripe documents an approval or feedback email in 4 business days, not guaranteed publication; changes to the app or listing require another review.

requirements: A Stripe account; live mode requires completing activation (verified business details)
OAuth enabled in Connect settings with at least one registered redirect URI (all URIs must be pre-registered)
Server-side storage for stripe_user_id per connected account; protect the platform API key
A webhook endpoint for account.application.deauthorized events
For marketplace publishing: test accounts, a reviewer-access route through MFA if enabled, testing guidance covering key features, and compliance with app requirements
nuances: Stripe explicitly does not recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms - Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts is the recommended path, so OAuth registration is mostly a legacy/extension concern.
Since June 2021, platforms using read_write scope cannot connect Standard accounts that are controlled by another platform; extensions are unaffected.
The scope rules are inverted from intuition: platforms must request read_write, and read_only exists only for registered extensions - omitting scope shows the user an error, not a consent screen.

The OAuth reference deprecates access_token and refresh_token in favor of platform API keys plus the Stripe-Account header. The onboarding guide still mentions refresh tokens; use the reference for current credential handling.

For marketplace apps, Stripe deprecated the Connect authentication method entirely: apps must use the marketplace OAuth v2 authorize URL, and reviewers install through your live-mode public install link.
Stripe documents a marketplace approval or feedback email in 4 business days. Feedback may require another submission, so this is not an end-to-end launch guarantee.

common_blockers.problem: The authorization page shows an error instead of a consent screen.
common_blockers.solution: The scope parameter is missing or read_only: platforms must pass scope=read_write explicitly. Also confirm the redirect_uri matches one pre-registered in Connect settings.

common_blockers.problem: Connecting a user's account fails for some users only.
common_blockers.solution: The docs say read_write platforms cannot connect Standard accounts controlled by another platform. Check the account-control situation and supported onboarding route rather than repeatedly retrying OAuth.

common_blockers.problem: Older examples suggest storing access and refresh tokens, but current response examples emphasize the account ID.
common_blockers.solution: Follow the OAuth reference: these token fields are deprecated. Store stripe_user_id and use the platform API key with Stripe-Account. Never exchange the same code twice; doing so revokes the connection.

common_blockers.problem: Marketplace review keeps coming back with feedback.
common_blockers.solution: Provide test accounts (never real accounts), explain how reviewers can pass MFA or disable it on the test accounts, and ensure test links connect through the app installation rather than Connect onboarding. Include testing guidance and recordings for complex flows; check the published quality requirements.

agent_can_do: Implement the full connection flow: authorize redirect with state, code exchange, Stripe-Account header usage, and deauthorize handling
Prefill the Stripe account form via stripe_user[...] parameters to cut onboarding drop-off
Set up the deauthorized webhook handler and cleanup logic
Draft the marketplace listing content and record the testing-guidance walkthroughs to the review checklist
human_must_do: Own the Stripe account and complete the applicable business and service activation requirements
Choose Connect onboarding versus Stripe Apps, and the test/live rollout
Approve the data access and distribution model; protect API credentials
Submit any marketplace listing and respond to feedback; the 4-business-day figure is for Stripe's decision email, not a deadline imposed on you

evidence.claim: Connect OAuth setup is self-serve in the dashboard: enable OAuth in the Connect OAuth onboarding options, copy the Stripe-generated client_id (separate live and test IDs), and pre-register all redirect URIs.

Stripe does not recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms (Connect Onboarding is recommended instead), and since June 2021 platforms using read_write scope cannot connect platform-controlled Standard accounts.
Platforms must pass scope=read_write; read_only is available only to registered extensions, and omitting scope or requesting read_only shows an error instead of the authorization page.

The OAuth reference deprecates access_token and refresh_token in favor of platform keys plus Stripe-Account. Token-exchange requests must match the code mode, and consuming a code more than once revokes the connection.
Live mode requires verifying the business and completing activation requirements; marketplace publishing requires a verified email and business details.

Marketplace publication requires review; Stripe documents an approval or feedback email in 4 business days. Reviewers need test accounts with MFA disabled or instructions to pass it, and test links must use app installation rather than Connect onboarding. The public install link uses marketplace OAuth v2.
The app review enforces qualitative requirements: transparent pricing, no ads, clear navigation without dead ends, real loading/error states, declared sandbox support in the manifest.
The Connect settings area of the Stripe dashboard resolves unauthenticated (the settings themselves sit behind login, like other providers' consoles).
Marketplace apps go through review; apps shared only with members of the same Stripe account do not. Private is the default distribution type.

uncertainties: How long account activation (business verification) takes is undocumented - it varies by country and business type, so the live-mode wait is unknown even though the marketplace review wait is not.

The Connect OAuth guide describes no separate app-review stage. It does not establish that all live platforms can connect accounts immediately; applicable activation, service and platform eligibility checks still need confirmation.
The June 2021 read_write restriction's exact definition of 'controlled by another platform' is not spelled out on the page - edge cases (migrated accounts, multiple platforms) are unclear.
The 4-business-day review timeline is stated for the initial decision email; total time-to-listing with feedback cycles is not bounded by the docs.
The Connect onboarding guide still describes refresh_token, while the OAuth reference marks it deprecated. This guide follows the reference and recommends account IDs with platform keys instead.
